conclusions: The selected policy loses in every frozen 2025 scenario. Its positive 2024 development result did not generalize to this confirmation window.
Entry activity stops through a continuous drawdown-scaled cap plus the joint minimum-lot/tracking-cost allocator. No drawdown, daily-loss, or accounting hard halt fired.
The final ETH short reduction occurs on May 10 at 19:00 UTC in base scenarios and 14:00 UTC in stress scenarios. Actual inventory remains zero for the rest of 2025.

After flattening, fixed cash keeps liquidation equity and its drawdown buffer unchanged. Daily-loss reset does not reset the peak-based drawdown cap. Fresh daily targets continue, but no target is executable at a better lot/cost objective.

At the first base hold, the BTC minimum lot exceeds the entire $3.252 cap. The feasible ETH minimum lot is about $2.501, but the desired short is only $1.183, below half a lot; flat minimizes tracking error before adding any trading costs.
ETH loses on price movement even before fees and funding. BTC base price earnings are smaller than its costs. Stress BTC is positive, but its gain does not offset ETH loss.
The two funding timestamp interpretations have identical position paths within each cost scenario. They change small funding cash amounts but do not explain or fix the confirmation stop.
Stress has higher costs and a different fixed execution delay, hence a different path; its smaller loss does not imply that increasing costs improves profitability.
A risk governor reduces exposure but cannot create a directional edge. The observed lot/cash feedback further limits subsequent participation; these results do not justify a profitability claim.
limitations: Hourly open execution remains a proxy; observed availability is replay-plan availability, not a claim about live quote health.
Both assets were flat by study end; six ETH held hours had zero-volume indicative marks. No missing exposed accounting path or zero-volume order attempt was reported.
Funding source timestamp convention remains unresolved; both fixed interpretations were retained.
The final 48 hours are a protocol flattening window; the stop occurred months earlier and is separately counted.
Price P&L uses simulated fill prices, so slippage is already reflected; it is not deducted twice.
